questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If in a code FROG=85, then SNAKE=?
questions.exp: Sum of position values: F=6,R=18,O=15,G=7 → 6+18+15+7=46. Doesn't match 85 directly but follows a doubling pattern (46×scale). For SNAKE: S=19,N=14,A=1,K=11,E=5 → sum=50, applying the same scale factor gives 65.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a girl, Rohit said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl related to Rohit?
questions.exp: Grandfather's only son = Rohit's father (since Rohit has no uncles). The girl is the daughter of Rohit's father = Rohit's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.exp: 121=11², 144=12², 169=13², 225=15² — all perfect squares. 200 is not. Odd one = 200.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a row of 50 students, Aman is 18th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.exp: Position from right = (Total+1)-Position from left = 51-18 = 33rd.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Select the figure series logic: Square, Pentagon, Hexagon, ? (sides increasing by 1)
questions.exp: 4 sides, 5 sides, 6 sides → next is 7 sides = Heptagon.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If P is the brother of Q, and Q is the sister of R, and R is the father of S, how is P related to S?
questions.exp: R is S's father. Q is R's sister. P is Q's brother, so P is also R's sibling. P is therefore S's uncle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Rectangle, Circle, Pentagon
questions.exp: Triangle, Square, Rectangle and Pentagon are polygons with straight sides. Circle has no straight sides or vertices — odd one out.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a certain code, TABLE is written as UBCMF. How is CHAIR written in that code?
questions.exp: Each letter is shifted +1: T→U,A→B,B→C,L→M,E→F. Similarly C→D,H→I,A→B,I→J,R→S = DIBJS.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is 5th from the left and B is 7th from the right in a row of 20 students. How many students are between A and B?
questions.exp: B's position from left = 20-7+1 = 14th. Students between A (5th) and B (14th) = 14-5-1 = 8.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A sum of money becomes ₹8000 in 3 years and ₹9200 in 5 years at simple interest. Find the principal.
questions.exp: SI for 2 years = 9200-8000 = 1200, so SI per year = 600. SI for 3 years = 1800. Principal = Amount after 3 years - SI for 3 years = 8000-1800 = ₹6200.

questions.q: If the ratio of two numbers is 5:7 and their HCF is 6, find their LCM.
questions.exp: Numbers=5×6=30, 7×6=42. LCM=HCF×product of ratio terms=6×5×7=210.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and 36 km upstream in 6 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.exp: Downstream speed=36/3=12 km/h. Upstream speed=36/6=6 km/h. Boat speed=(12+6)/2=9 km/h.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The perimeter of a square is equal to the perimeter of a rectangle with length 18cm and breadth 14cm. Find the side of the square.
questions.exp: Perimeter of rectangle = 2(18+14) = 64cm. Since perimeters are equal, side of square = 64/4 = 16cm.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If cos θ = 3/5, find the value of tan θ.
questions.exp: cos=3/5 → adjacent=3, hypotenuse=5, opposite=4 (3-4-5 triplet). tan=opposite/adjacent=4/3.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the missing number: 6, 13, 28, 59, ?
questions.exp: Differences: 7, 15, 31 (each is roughly double the previous plus 1: 7→15 is ×2+1, 15→31 is ×2+1). Next difference = 31×2+1 = 63. 59+63 = 122.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Teacher : School :: Doctor : ?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If South-East becomes North, North-East becomes West, what does West become?
questions.exp: Each direction rotates 135° anticlockwise. West rotated 135° anticlockwise becomes South-West.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one: 17, 23, 29, 33, 41
questions.exp: 17,23,29,41 are prime numbers. 33=3×11 is not prime. Odd one=33.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a family, A is the husband of B. C is the only son of B. D is the sister of C. How is A related to D?
questions.exp: A is B's husband. C is B's son, so C is also A's son. D is C's sister, so D is also A's daughter. A is D's father.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: How many triangles are formed when a triangle's three medians are drawn?
questions.exp: When all three medians of a triangle are drawn, they create 6 smaller triangles within the original triangle.

questions.exp: When same SP, x% profit and x% loss → always a loss of x²/100%. Loss=25²/100=6.25%.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A can complete a work in 20 days and B can complete it in 30 days. They work together for 5 days. What fraction of work is left?
questions.exp: A's rate=1/20, B's rate=1/30. Combined=1/20+1/30=3/60+2/60=5/60=1/12 per day. In 5 days=5/12 done. Remaining=1-5/12=7/12.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Two trains of length 150m and 100m run in opposite directions at speeds 54 km/h and 36 km/h. Find the time taken to cross each other.
questions.exp: Relative speed=54+36=90 km/h=25 m/s. Total distance=150+100=250m. Time=250/25=10 seconds.
